prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” truck-accident lawyer for everyone — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your case, your injuries, the parties involved, and how you want the case handled (settlement vs. trial). Instead of one name, here’s how to find the best lawyer for your truck accident in Dallas and what to do next.

How to pick the right Dallas truck-accident lawyer
- Relevant experience: Look for lawyers who handle truck (not just car) collisions regularly and understand trucking rules (FMCSA, hours-of-service, logbooks, maintenance, etc.).  
- Trial experience: Trucking companies often fight claims aggressively. Prefer a lawyer who has taken cases to trial and obtained verdicts.  
- Resources and experts: The attorney should have access to accident reconstructionists, mechanics, medical experts, and investigators.  
- Track record: Ask about prior settlements/verdicts in truck cases and case results similar to yours (not every case is identical).  
- Board certification and memberships: In Texas, board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (Texas Board of Legal Specialization) is a strong plus. Memberships in TTLA or AAJ are useful indicators.  
- Communication and availability: You want timely updates and a clear point of contact.  
- Contingency fee and costs: Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency; confirm the percentage, how expenses are handled, and whether you’ll owe anything if you lose.  
- Local reputation and reviews: Check client reviews, Martindale-Hubbell/Avvo ratings, and peer-reviewed recognitions.  

Where to search and verify
- State Bar of Texas Lawyer Referral or Search (to confirm license and discipline history)  
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board-certified trial lawyers)  
- Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA) and American Association for Justice (AAJ) member lists  
- Google/Yelp reviews, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo — check both client reviews and peer ratings

Questions to ask at an initial consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many in the last 3 years?  
- Have you represented plaintiffs against large trucking companies/insurers? Do you have trial experience in these cases?  
- Who will handle the case day-to-day — you or an associate?  
- What is your strategy for a case like mine? How long might it take?  
- What experts will you use (accident reconstruction, trucking operations, medicine)?  
- How are fees and costs handled (contingency %, who advances expenses)?  
- Can you provide references from past truck-accident clients?  

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report, photos/videos of the scene and vehicles, contact info for witnesses  
- Medical records and bills, list of injuries and treatment timeline  
- Insurance information (your own and the truck’s, if known)  
- Any correspondence from insurers, employers, or the trucking company

Immediate steps if you were recently injured
- Seek and document medical care right away. Medical records are critical.  
- Preserve evidence (photos, video, location, vehicle damage).  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the trucking company or their insurer without an attorney.  
- Note witness names and contact info.  
- Be mindful of Texas’s statute of limitations for personal injury — generally 2 years from the date of the crash.

If you want, I can:
- Help you prepare a short list of targeted questions for consultations.  
- Draft an email/phone script to contact attorneys.  
- Review the answers or retainer offers you receive and point out areas to watch.

If you’d like a shortlist of reputable Dallas truck-accident lawyers, tell me any preferences (trial-focused, budget concerns, severe injuries, bilingual) and whether you want me to draft messages you can send to attorneys.
